questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not have many requirements for choosing Greenland. To me the location mattered more than the subjects. There were not many subjects to choose from, but Greenland has so much to offer. A lovely people, beautiful nature, and a more calm society than in Denmark, which was crucial for me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The experience was overall great. I met new friends, got to explore the country, and the people here are just generally very nice. The exchange coordinator at the university, was phenomenal at welcoming us and helping us getting the best experience. He booked a fishing trip for us, we had coffee and cake at the university every other friday, and there was even an international kaffemik, where we all had to bring our own dish to serve for the university.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy because of the exchange coordinator at the university of Ilisimatusarfik

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Same as I have written above. The coordinator also helped us getting submitted to the right classes, and removed again if the class was not fitting, or taught in Greenlandic.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: As I have mentioned in the previous text boxes, the help and assistance have been great. Very quick response, and you were always met with a smile.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is not easy to find housing here in Nuuk. The exchange coordinator sends a link to a website where you have to submit an application for a dorm, kollegie. There are not many dorms for the amount of people applying, so in the beginning my application was declined. However, right before leaving for Greenland, I sent a new application, which was accepted, and the same happened to some other exchange students from my group. Also, the dorms here are very cheap. The price is 869 DKK for everything, except for internet.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The rent is very cheap, but other costs will come up, for instance internet/wifi which is very expensive. It is generally nice to live off campus, because you get to live with other people in a big apartment.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is good, but not super clean when you arrive, and we had troubles with the radiator

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Once again, our exchange coordinator was very helpful and made whole process super easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You submitted an application, and then a few months later got a reply. Then all through summer, our coordinator helped us with login to Lectio, the platform used at the university, he helped us with the housing, and basically everything. Once arrived, we received the university card, and he helped us further with everything

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Same as written above

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was succesful. The classes are not very full, so you will be registered in all the classes you want

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about it. Help will be offered.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic program in Greenland was not the best, but with good reason. Most of our teachers had to come up from Denmark and would only be there for a week, where we'd have intensive back to back classes. The rest of the time, the classes was online. However the teachers were very professional and great.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is quite easy coming from Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A other of online classes, and less participation in some of the classes. For instance we did not have to prepare group presentations like we did in the university of Copenhagen

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Criminal law in danish
International law in danish
Human rights in danish
Civil rights in danish

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend Criminal law. In greenland it is called kriminalret, and in Denmark "strafferet". It is two different kinds of systems, and I found it interesting to learn about the difference.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Unexpected cost was the internet in the dorm

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Wifi and data was super expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There weren't much at the university. I was really missing that. Although it is possible to attend private sports etc.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Not much. They had some get together things once in a while in the canteen, but nothing special.
As an exchange student some extra things were planned for us which was nice

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take a trip to Ilulissat with the ferry, or maybe other places, be active and search for things that are happening in the town. Go out to eat. Go to the pubquiz every thursday at Daddy's (the local pub where all young people will attend)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Same as above

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I have lived here before and am thriving in this calm environment.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open, and positive

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The locals students are very quiet, and it can be hard to get to know them

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are all super welcoming and happy

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: If you plan on going to Greenland, don't go here only for an academic purpose. The university here is not near as good as you would see in Denmark, and I experienced a lot of the other students getting disappointed, because they had expected more. If you chose to go to Greenland it should be for the experience, the culture, living abroad, meeting new people, and exploring an absolutely stunning country with plenty of opportunities for hiking, fishing, hunting etc.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Apply for dorms right after the exchange coordinator has given you the link.
As a student from the university of Copenhagen you will not be given the Nord Plus scholarship, so make sure to apply in advance for scholarships

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The overall experience. It was truly amazing, and I recommend everyone to come here

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not getting the Nordplus legat as a student from The University of Copenhagen. They don't give them out at all, so it was very financially expensive

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
